VERDICT: POSITIVE - THE ROUTE EXISTS. This is the answer to the whole investigation.
headline: MEGAcmd downloads a public folder link with NO ACCOUNT, and DECRYPTS the contents correctly. Every earlier route died on the HTTP 402 proof-of-work or on the missing file key. megacmd is MEGA's own official client, so it solves the 402 - and being the client, it is also the thing that performs the decryption.

installation.why_wsl: Linux is the intended target (a VPS), so this is the representative environment - and it avoids installing a Windows background service on the operator's machine.
installation.scoop_attempt_failed: The scoop manifest for megacmd 2.6.0 carries the URL 'https://mega.nz/MEGAcmdSetup.exe#/dl.7z', which is invalid - the '#' makes it unservable. A manifest bug, not a MEGA problem.
installation.apt_repo_attempt_failed: MEGA's documented apt host eu.repo.mega.co.nz NO LONGER RESOLVES in DNS. WSL networking itself is fine - mega.nz returned HTTP 200 in 0.62s and github resolved - so this is a dead host, not a network fault.
installation.working_source: Direct .deb from MEGA's own download page: https://mega.nz/linux/repo/xUbuntu_26.04/amd64/megacmd-xUbuntu_26.04_amd64.deb

anonymous_access_PROVEN.shell_commands: mega-ls and other shell commands report 'Not logged in.' - they require a session.
anonymous_access_PROVEN.exported_link_command: mega-get is the documented command for exported links and it works with NO account, exactly as MEGA's UserGuide states: 'you can download public links or upload to public folders without logging in.'
anonymous_access_PROVEN.result: HTTP 200 equivalent - content transferred, no credentials of any kind involved

decryption_PROVEN.method: Content was inspected, not merely size-matched. A correct byte count could still be ciphertext, so plaintext had to be demonstrated.

text_file.file_type: ASCII text, with no line terminators
text_file.VERDICT: VALID PLAINTEXT. The file is decrypted and human-readable.

known_limitation_found.issue: The '::' subpath syntax was NOT honoured. Requesting a single file caused megacmd to begin fetching the ENTIRE share.
known_limitation_found.consequence: The download cannot be scoped to a subfolder. A naive 'mega-get <link>' pulls all 319.95 GB.
known_limitation_found.mitigation_available: megacmd provides a streaming interface (stream / webdav) which yields a file without storing it, so the full corpus need never be staged on disk even on the VPS.
known_limitation_found.safety_net_used_in_this_probe: A hard 'timeout 45' bounded the test; 84 files / 13 MB landed before it fired, and the post-check reported the actual bytes so a runaway was DETECTED rather than assumed impossible.

final_architecture.shape: VPS (Linux): megacmd streams a public-link file -> POST to Deepgram -> discard. PC receives transcript JSON only.
final_architecture.closed_api_required: NO - the 402 proof-of-work is irrelevant because the official client solves it
final_architecture.local_ffmpeg_required: NO - Deepgram accepts MP4 containers (proven separately by an equivalence test)
final_architecture.disk_on_vps_required: NO if the streaming interface is used; YES (312 GB) if mega-get is used wholesale
final_architecture.vendor_spend: Deepgram only, already waived at a measured USD 136.31 forecast, plus the VPS itself.

what_each_earlier_attempt_had_already_es.corpus_measured: 38 folders, 198 calls, 528.35 audio hours, 312.16 GB reconciled - obtained through the official web client, which is why it remains valid.
what_each_earlier_attempt_had_already_es.deepgram_accepted: MP4 container ACCEPTED (WAV and MP4 gave identical utterance/paragraph/word counts). URL fetch SUPPORTED. Consent gate PASS.
what_each_earlier_attempt_had_already_es.call_join: 198 calls, 44 carrying an AI Summary, 7 recorded orphans under the slot rule.

probe_bytes: 13 MB of small files into WSL during the bounded test; no corpus audio was touched.
